data.desc: `viola open` — a terminal window per session beside its parent, closed allowlist, no shell; window and origin recorded by the wrapper

body:
**Working entry (verbatim):** «`viola open` — a terminal window per session beside its parent; closed flag allowlist,
no shell; window identity and origin in its own state, logged codes-only». The entry carries three carries (`block`
view, `chk-gvely5gr`): `cry-fhabylf6`, `cry-pu3g6nb7`, `cry-2oejf2md`, each folded below and each disposed by name
(directive item 1). The marker takes `-2`: the cancelled take-up's journal file `2026-11-23T12-02-59-2026-11-23-viola-open.ndjson`
stands committed (promotion.md §Marker).

**Capabilities:** v2-07 «Launch a session into the fleet», claimed GATED on R2; v2-08 «The launch authority bounded»,
planned to verify on the fake (carry `cry-fhabylf6`, the operator's own answer F9). Nothing wider.

- **The verb `viola open`** (v2-07, v2-08; the operator's own answers F1 · F2 · F4 · F6 · F8 and the split F9, and the
  overseer's technical F3 · F5 · F7, cited from `split-carry.md` §4 and re-asked of nobody — directive item 2):
  - **Arguments (F1):** `<name>`, `--parent`, `--role overseer|builder|worker` (closed), `--cwd`, `--workspace N`,
    `--model` / `--effort`, `--json`, `--home`; after `--` the word `claude` alone, with no claude flag. A flag outside
    the allowlist is refused before anything starts (v2-08).
  - **Terminal (F2):** `foot` found on PATH and started directly, no shell; argv `foot --app-id=viola.<name>
    --title=<name> --working-directory=<cwd> <pinned viola> --home <home> run <name> …`. No shell line is built from
    the arguments, whatever characters they hold (v2-08).
  - **Placement (F3 · F4 · F5):** viola reads `clients` until a window's pid is the terminal's, then issues the ONE
    closed move dispatch the seam chunk landed, moving that address to the parent's workspace (or `--workspace N`);
    the layout decides the neighbour, no focus change. No parent window → no move, recorded `unplaced`. Off Hyprland
    (the seam's own `unsupported` / `unreachable`, no environment read) the terminal still starts, placement skipped,
    the record says why. On a locked desktop the open proceeds.
  - **Liveness and bounds (F8):** open returns once the instance is live (`viola_state::liveness::live_endpoint`),
    waiting at most 30 s, else exit 1 `not-live` with the window left standing; the window's appearance gets 5 s
    (polling `clients` at 100 ms), then `unplaced`. Each new bound lands as a row of its own beside the full
    time-bound lists.
  - **Words and exits (F6):** exit 2 outside the allowlist (clap's usage error, plus one fixed line for a word after
    `--` other than `claude`, beside `PAIR_AFTER_DASHES`); exit 1 `terminal-not-found`; exit 1 `not-live`;
    `already-live` / `stale-heartbeat` read before any spawn; exit 1 `strict-modes-failed` before any log; no exit 11;
    `--json` `{"v":1,"ok":{"name","parent","window","placement"}}` / `{"v":1,"error":"<code>","detail":null}`; help
    `setup:  open, run, revive, verify, plugin install`.
  - **Parent default:** the parent defaults to the caller's `VIOLA_NAME` when an agent calls open from its own shell.

- **The window record (F7):** the wrapper records its own window, never the open (only the wrapper writes
  `snapshot.json` and its start lines — split-carry §3, premise-corrected). Open hands its origin (`cli` · `agent`) on
  the started `viola run`'s argv through one hidden checked flag; the wrapper finds its window by its terminal
  ancestor's pid through the seam. A new log-only kind `window {address?, workspace?, placement, origin}` and a
  snapshot `window?`, replayed with the last line winning; `list --json` gains `window?` / `origin?`; the six-column
  board stays unchanged. Logged codes-only.

- **The recorder's three untested codes** (carry `cry-pu3g6nb7`): tests for `viola-hypr-tap`'s `record-move` failure
  codes `move-refused`, `move-unseen` and `window-left`, with no live window, over the planted stubs
  `crates/viola-e2e/tests/hypr_tap.rs` already uses. [inferred] each is reachable over a stub as the carry names it.

- **`HYPRCTL_DEADLINE` as an a11y time-bound row** (carry `cry-2oejf2md`): the settled 5 s compositor read bound joins
  the a11y time-bound rows (`decision/time-bounds-fall-on-the-driver` / `-never-on-human`) as a row of its own, with
  this chunk — the seam's first product caller.

- **R2, the one live reading, is the stop** (carry `cry-fhabylf6`, F9): ONE `viola open` end to end beside a live
  parent under a scratch home (outside every repository, a private `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`), at the operator's host,
  unlocked, its moment his to name and not given. It gates v2-07. Implement builds and greens everything that does not
  need R2, makes the pre-CI commit, and STOPS once before R2 (directive item 5).

body:
# Phase directive — «`viola open`» (Epoch 5, viola-0.2.0; the head entry `chk-gvely5gr` at `d7b65a6d`)

**WHAT IS AN INPUT, AND WHAT IS NOT.** Of the folder this directive stands in, the ONLY files you read or snap are
this directive and the relay files a later send names. Nothing else under it is read, cited or snapped. A fact the
plan needs and this directive does not state is ASKED of the overseer in the P3 block, never looked up.

The operator answers through the overseer: raise NO question dialog for him. A fork that is his is written to
`{run_dir}/founder-forks.md` (the question, the options in order with each one's cost, the recommendation marked)
and the step stops there, saying so. A technical fork is answered by the overseer's relay at once. **This phase
makes NO live start, opens, moves, focuses or closes NO window, sends NO key, and reads nothing of the operator's
real `~/.claude*`.** In your chat messages name a compiled screen literal, never print it.

## Facts, measured by the overseer 2026-11-23T21:22Z — cite them as this directive's

- The tree at `d7b65a6d` = its upstream: position 131 records, 131 complete, 0 pending, 0 gated; coverage of
  viola-0.2.0 `verified 25/37 · deferred 2 · planned 10`. The route's next entry is `chk-gvely5gr` «`viola open`»,
  its hint verbatim: «a terminal window per session beside its parent; closed flag allowlist, no shell; window
  identity and origin in its own state, logged codes-only». It carries THREE carries: `cry-fhabylf6` (the
  operator's answers F1 · F2 · F4 · F6 · F8 and the split F9, NOT re-asked; R2 gates v2-07; `split-carry.md` of
  run `2026-11-23T12-02-15Z-phase` is an input of this phase), `cry-pu3g6nb7` (tests for the recorder's
  `move-refused`, `move-unseen`, `window-left` over planted stubs) and `cry-2oejf2md` (the settled
  `HYPRCTL_DEADLINE` joins the a11y time-bound rows as a row of its own, with the seam's first product caller).
- `split-carry.md` reads back whole by the install's `rec.py runs --root . --kind 2026-11-23T12-02-15Z-phase
  --file split-carry.md --show` (sealed, 18232 B): its §1 measurements, §2 what «verified» rests on per clause,
  §4 every answer F1–F9 with the overseer's technical F3 · F5 · F7, §5 the reached rows, §6 disk, SIGKILL and
  the test children. It was written at `ddf3b411`, BEFORE «Seam requests for viola open» landed: every count in
  it about the seam (requests, words, fixtures, the deadline's state) is re-measured at HEAD, not copied.
- A bare `claude` on this host is 2.1.330 and this session runs it `verified`. `hyprctl locked` read `false` at
  21:22:47Z; that reading grants nothing — the operator is not at the host for this phase.
- Another project builds on this host from 21:22Z for hours: a gate red with no failed assertion is read against
  `python3 ~/dev/projects/additional/andromedaV3/andromeda-overseer/docs/tools/hostwatch.py read --from <the
  entry's start> --to <now>` first and never re-run for green; read `df -m /tmp` beside it.

## The directive

1. Scope is the route entry as it stands at `d7b65a6d`, its three carries and v2-07 / v2-08, nothing wider. Every
   carry is disposed by name — taken, or left with its reason and its next owner. v2-08 is planned to verify on
   the fake; v2-07 is claimed GATED on R2. Say at P1, per clause, what «verified» rests on, re-read against
   `split-carry.md` §2 and the tree at HEAD.
2. **The operator's answers F1 · F2 · F4 · F6 · F8 · F9 and the overseer's F3 · F5 · F7 BIND the plan.** They are
   cited from `split-carry.md` §4 and re-asked of nobody. A place where the tree at HEAD makes one of them
   impossible or ambiguous is a fork: his where it moves his answer, technical otherwise — say which, with the
   measurement.
3. **Measurements first, at P3, each a number or a closed word from a test, a no-start and no-window probe, the
   recorded fixtures or a read-only compositor query:** what the seam holds at HEAD (its requests, words,
   fixtures, the deadline) against `split-carry.md` §1; what the recorded move fixture says of the dispatch's
   argv and reply; which of §5's reached rows still read as reached and which rows the seam chunk's wrap already
   moved. Say what stays the fake's and unmeasured live.
4. **Search ALL seven masters again before the block is written** — by the counted literals a row or a test pins
   (start-record counts, event kinds, the verb table, exit-cause tables, config keys, the board's columns) and by
   «replays no», «never», «only» — and name every reached row with the read-not-reached ones beside them. Order
   the searches re-run before the whole layers. A new time bound whose list cell is full lands as a row of its
   own; no member's words shortened.
5. **R2 is ONE named step that implement STOPS before**, with everything that does not need R2 built and green
   and the pre-CI commit made before that stop. The plan names for R2: what it opens, how many times, the scratch
   home (outside every repository, a private `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`), what it needs ABSENT or PRESENT on disk
   outside the tree and the no-start entry that reads it, what it leaves behind and how each thing is closed, and
   which reading turns it red. R2 runs only on the operator's own word at the host, unlocked, under his cap.
6. **At P3's END, before P4:** write ONE block in `founder-forks.md` — your window, the measurements, every
   reached row, any fork of his with its options priced, any NEW closed word, exit, bound, record field or
   `--json` member beyond `split-carry.md` §4, and whether one implement window holds the entry. **If the block
   holds NO fork of his, say so in its first line and go on to P4 without waiting.**
7. Say what each new record writes to DISK, what outlives a SIGKILL, and what of a parent's identity lands where
   another session or a public tree can read it — re-read against §6, and name what moved.
8. A new test child or fake-agent behaviour is named, with the case that proves it and the bound every waiting
   test takes under the 20 s lint. Every TEST start runs under a test-owned user home.
9. Every `gate.py control` has an id of 1–16 characters, its `--timeout S`, and an entry filtered to its guard's
   own cases that builds the whole workspace where the case needs a root binary. Every filter term SELECTS at
   least one test under its layer flag. An expect atom must be able to fail; a word that may honestly read two
   ways is a READING recorded; an after-read of state OTHER actors move is keyed to the round leg; no gate entry
   asserts a state a later step of the same plan ends. A test that skips prints its reason.
10. No mutation run. Read `df` before a whole rebuild. A fold is decided at the PHASE. A guard's or the permission
    classifier's refusal is never routed around: stop and tell the overseer. On an account-limit refusal, stop.
11. Call NO scheduled-wake or timer tool. End every process you start; remove no scratch clone by a recursive
    delete — name it on the card. Leaves hold no figure the code states.
12. Run the phase exactly as the letters say, read as they stand. On the P5 card, in one block, verbatim where a
    tool printed it: the union's per-master lines and the `rows-union` line; whether EVERY cited row is in the
    union or its standing list; the round pre-flight's lines if the plan holds a round; every `[RETYPED]` line
    and re-spawn; every non-zero exit, refusal, `UNPARSED` / `INDETERMINATE` / `NOT DERIVED` line; every place a
    letter was wrong or silent.

data.head: ## Measurements at HEAD `d7b65a6d` (directive item 3; each re-run, never copied from split-carry §1)

body:
- **M1 · the seam's set** — `crates/viola-hyprland/src/lib.rs@d7b65a6d`: `Request` holds 8 requests, 5 queries
  (`Clients`, `ActiveWindow`, `Workspaces`, `Version`, `Monitors`) and 3 dispatches (`FocusWindow`, `Workspace`,
  `MoveToWorkspace`; `is_dispatch`, lib.rs:111-116); `WORDS` 8 words (lib.rs:120-129); `HyprlandError` 5 words
  (`unsupported` · `unreachable` · `oversize` · `malformed` · `refused`, lib.rs:132-145). split-carry §1.1 read 6 · 6 ·
  5: the seam chunk added `monitors` and `move-to-workspace`.

- **M2 · the deadline** — `crates/viola-hyprland/src/read.rs:21` `HYPRCTL_DEADLINE = 5 s`, its doc comment «settled
  (security-plan, the hyprctl read deadline)»; the security row `decision/hyprctl-read-deadline` stands with guard
  `read_past_the_deadline_kills_and_reaps_its_child` and no `provisional` tag (security rows file). split-carry §1.1
  read PROVISIONAL: moved by the seam chunk's wrap.

- **M3 · fixtures** — `ls fixtures/hyprland/0.56.2/`: 9 files (`ActiveWindow`, `Clients`, `FocusWindow`, `Monitors`,
  `MoveToWorkspace`, `Version`, `Version.absent`, `Workspace`, `Workspaces`). split-carry read 7.

- **M4 · the move fixture's argv and reply** — `fixtures/hyprland/0.56.2/MoveToWorkspace.recorded-1.json`: `args`
  `["dispatch", "hl.dsp.window.move({ workspace = 1, window = \"address:0x555aa16bde50\" })"]`, `exit` 0, `stdout`
  `"ok\n"` (R1's recording). The fake hyprctl replays only an exact argv (`src/bin/viola-fake-agent/hyprctl.rs`
  `hyprctl_output`, an argv no fixture holds → no output, exit 1), so a replayed move must name that address and
  workspace 1.

- **M5 · no product caller** — `Cargo.toml:174` holds `viola-hyprland` under `[dev-dependencies]`; a grep of
  `viola_hyprland` over `src/` and `crates/viola-*/src` (the seam crate aside) hits `src/obs.rs:30` (the log-target
  list) and `crates/viola-e2e/src/bin/viola-hypr-tap.rs` only. The graph's `viola → viola-hyprland` edge is the root
  tests' (crate_edges query).

- **M6 · host, read-only** — `hyprctl -j version`: tag `v0.56.2`, commit `efb50993`; `command -v foot` →
  `/usr/bin/foot`, `foot --version` 1.28.0. No window opened, moved or focused; no dispatch.

- **M7 · the tap's three untested codes** — `crates/viola-e2e/src/bin/viola-hypr-tap.rs:244-276` `record_move`:
  `move-refused` when the move's reply is not `Reply::Dispatched`; `move-unseen` when the terminal's window does not read
  the target workspace after it; `window-left` when the ended terminal's pid is still listed after `WINDOW_WAIT`
  (5 s, polled at `WINDOW_POLL` 100 ms, lines 48-49). `crates/viola-e2e/tests/hypr_tap.rs` `stub_move` (lines 95-118)
  plants a shell `hyprctl` whose dispatch prints `ok` and whose `clients` follows `/proc/$pid`: each code is reachable
  with a stub variant (a dispatch printing another text; a dispatch not writing `moved`; a `clients` that lists the pid
  whatever `/proc` says). Carry `cry-pu3g6nb7` verified.

- **M8 · liveness** — `viola_state::liveness::live_endpoint` (callers: 7 CLI verbs + MCP, graph query) gives an
  endpoint only for a real snapshot with the same pid and start time and a beat ≤ `STALE_AFTER` (5 s).

- **M9 · the automatic verify runs only with `verify_new_cli` on** — `src/run/auto_verify.rs:21-46`: `config.json`'s
  `verify_new_cli`, absent `false`. A home with no `config.json` runs no automatic verify; an unverified CLI starts
  transport-only and writes no trust record (`src/cmd/run.rs:514-517`).

- **M10 · the start order** — `src/cmd/run.rs:346-504` `start`: resolve program → collision check → pin + plugin →
  version gate → bind → automatic verify → trust step → slots → serve → `start_state` (first snapshot, heartbeat,
  `wheel` · `lineage` · `launch` lines, run.rs:652-694) → `spawn_child`.

- **M11 · the lineage default** — `src/cmd/run.rs:115` `lineage_of(args, client::own_name())`: `--parent`, else the
  inherited `VIOLA_NAME`, dropped when equal to the instance; `checked` (run.rs:99-110) refuses a self parent and a
  pair after `--` (exit 2, `PAIR_AFTER_DASHES`, `src/run/launch.rs:109`).

- **What stays the fake's, unmeasured live** — the window's map time after foot's spawn; whether foot maps its window
  before its child runs; a locked desktop's effect on a new window; the move on a window viola's product opened (R1
  moved the tap's own window, not a product one). R2 measures the end-to-end open; nothing else here is live.
- `crates/viola-hyprland/src/lib.rs` (full) — the closed set, `Address`, `WorkspaceId`, `WORDS`, `HyprlandError`.
- `crates/viola-hyprland/src/read.rs` (1-120) — `read`, `HYPRCTL_DEADLINE`, the spawn pair `hyprctl-probe`.
- `fixtures/hyprland/0.56.2/MoveToWorkspace.recorded-1.json` (full) — M4.
- `src/bin/viola-fake-agent/hyprctl.rs` (1-80) — the file-name dispatch, `hyprctl-mode`, exact-argv replay.
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/bin/viola-hypr-tap.rs` (220-290) — `record_move`, `within`, the three codes.
- `crates/viola-e2e/tests/hypr_tap.rs` (84-330) — `stub_terminal`, `stub_move`, the two record-move tests.
- `src/cmd/mod.rs` (full) — `HELP_TEMPLATE`, `Command`, `dispatch`, `instance_of`, `resolved_home`.
- `src/cmd/run.rs` (44-130, 240-800) — `RunArgs`, `checked`, `lineage_of`, `start`, `start_state`, `collision_check`.
- `src/run/launch.rs` (full) — the pair, `PAIR_AFTER_DASHES`, `names_pair`.
- `src/run/auto_verify.rs` (1-60), `src/run/version_gate.rs` (161-200) — M9.
- `crates/viola-state/src/snapshot.rs` (39-80) — `InstanceSnapshot`, `Launch`.
- `crates/viola-core/src/lib.rs` (58-100, 630-640) — `EventKind`, the kind/key table test.
- `crates/viola-state/src/board.rs` (grep) — the `model`/`effort` item fields, the model-word re-parse.
- `schemas/diag-line.v1.json` (66-77) — `subject` ref, `process-exit` `detail` enum.
- `Cargo.toml` (160-176, 237) — M5; `sysinfo` a normal dependency of `viola-state` only.

- **viola-hyprland** — inbound crate edges `viola-e2e` and `viola` (tests), outbound `viola-core` only: the chunk makes
  `viola` a product consumer (a `[dependencies]` entry).

- **live_endpoint** — 7 product callers (`src/cmd/{answer,last,link,pause,send,wait}.rs`, `crates/viola-mcp/src/tools.rs`)
  unchanged; `open` becomes an eighth, read-only, after its own strict-modes check.

data.head: ## Design reading the plan leans on (closed at P3; the technical forks of `founder-forks.md`)

body:
- **T1 · who finds and moves the window.** F3 (open reads `clients` for the terminal's pid and moves) and F7 (the
  wrapper records `window {…, placement, origin}`) are jointly unsatisfiable as written: the placement is known only to
  the process that moves, and only the wrapper writes the record (test-plan decision/single-writer-state-files). Lean
  ★: the wrapper finds its window by its parent pid (`std::os::unix::process::parent_id`, the foot process F2 spawns
  it under) through the seam, moves it, and records it; `open` computes the target workspace before the spawn and
  hands it with the origin on the started `run`'s argv.

- **T2 · the target's carrier.** Lean ★: two hidden checked `run` flags, `--origin cli|agent` and `--place <N>`
  (an `i32`); F7 named one. The alternative is one flag carrying both words.

- **T3 · the parent's window.** Lean ★: the parent snapshot's recorded `window.address`, its workspace read from
  `clients`; with none, the parent wrapper's pid and its ancestors (sysinfo, at most 8 steps) matched against
  `clients`' `pid`; neither → no target, `unplaced`.

- **T4 · where the window step stands.** Lean ★: in the wrapper's start, after the automatic verify and the trust
  step, before the first snapshot — only under `--origin`; the first snapshot holds `window`, and its `window` line
  follows `launch`, so «live» implies «window recorded». The claude spawn waits up to the 5 s window bound.

- **T5 · the pinned viola on foot's argv.** Lean ★: `open` pins its own bytes into the home through the start's
  `pin_bytes` (placed new, re-hashed on reuse) and hands that absolute path.

- **T6 · the replay's window rule.** Lean ★: the last `window` line after the last `launch` line wins; a later
  start's `launch` line clears it (a revive or plain start records no window).
- `src/cmd/open.rs` — the `open` verb: args, checks, target workspace, foot spawn, the live wait, `--json`.
- `src/run/window.rs` — the wrapper's window step: find by parent pid, move, the `window` record.

- `src/bin/viola-fake-agent/foot.rs` — the fake agent standing as `foot`: runs its trailing argv as its direct child, an
  argv receipt beside its exe.
- `tests/cli_open.rs` — the open verb end to end over the fake foot, the fake hyprctl and the fake agent.
- `Cargo.toml` — `viola-hyprland` moves to `[dependencies]` of the root bin.
- `src/cmd/mod.rs` — the `Open` command, its dispatch and sink, `HELP_TEMPLATE`'s `setup:` row.
- `src/cmd/run.rs` — hidden `--origin` / `--place`, the window step in `start`, `Recorded`/`start_state` window.
- `src/run/mod.rs` — the `window` module.
- `crates/viola-core/src/lib.rs` — `EventKind::Window` and its keys, the placement and origin words.
- `crates/viola-state/src/snapshot.rs` — the `Window` record and the snapshot's `window` field.
- `crates/viola-state/src/replay.rs` — the window rule.
- `crates/viola-state/src/board.rs` — the item's `window` / `origin`.
- `crates/viola-state/src/liveness.rs` — the ancestor pids of a pid (T3).
- `crates/viola-core/src/obs.rs` — the `terminal` spawn subject and the open's exit details.
- `schemas/diag-line.v1.json` — subject `terminal`, details `terminal-not-found` and `not-live`.
- `src/human/hints.rs` — the two new refusal pairs.
- `src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs` — the `foot` file-name dispatch.
- `src/bin/viola-fake-agent/hyprctl.rs` — a `terminal` mode: a `clients` reply naming the stand-in terminal's pid.
- `crates/viola-e2e/tests/hypr_tap.rs` — the three record-move code tests (carry `cry-pu3g6nb7`).
- `tests/cli_output_plain.rs` — the `HELP` literal.
- `tests/cross_exit_causes.rs` — the two exit-1 codes.
- `tests/contract_error_bodies.rs` — the open's documents.
- `tests/contract_diag_schema.rs` — the new subject and details.
- `HELP_TEMPLATE|setup:    run` over `src/` and `tests/`: re-run at P4 by name (the `HELP` literal's sites).

- `viola_hyprland` over `src/` and `crates/viola-*/src`: 2 hits · 0 changed · 2 no-change (the log-target list; the
  test-only tap) — M5.
- T1–T6 → blocks: plan-decision — answered by the overseer's relay if he moves a lean; the plan is written on the ★ leans.

- **The verb `viola open`** (v2-07, v2-08; the operator's own answers F1 · F2 · F4 · F6 · F8 and the split F9, and the
  overseer's technical F3 · F5 · F7, cited from `split-carry.md` §4 and re-asked of nobody — directive item 2):
  - **Arguments (F1):** `<name>`, `--parent`, `--role overseer|builder|worker` (closed), `--cwd`, `--workspace N`,
    `--model` / `--effort`, `--json`, `--home`; after `--` the word `claude` alone, with no claude flag. A flag outside
    the allowlist is refused before anything starts (v2-08).
  - **Terminal (F2):** `foot` found on PATH and started directly, no shell; argv `foot --app-id=viola.<name>
    --title=<name> --working-directory=<cwd> <pinned viola> --home <home> run <name> …`. No shell line is built from
    the arguments, whatever characters they hold (v2-08).
  - **Placement (F3 · F4 · F5):** [premise-corrected: F3's mover and F7's recorder are jointly unsatisfiable as
    written — the placement is known only to the process that moves, and only the wrapper writes the record; research
    T1–T6] the wrapper, under the hidden flags `open` hands it, reads `clients` until a window's pid is its parent's
    (the foot process F2 spawns it under), then issues the ONE closed move dispatch the seam chunk landed, moving that
    address to the target `open` computed before the spawn — the parent's workspace (its recorded window, else its
    wrapper's ancestor pids matched against `clients`) or `--workspace N`;
    the layout decides the neighbour, no focus change. No parent window → no move, recorded `unplaced`. Off Hyprland
    (the seam's own `unsupported` / `unreachable`, no environment read) the terminal still starts, placement skipped,
    the record says why. On a locked desktop the open proceeds.
  - **Liveness and bounds (F8):** open returns once the instance is live (`viola_state::liveness::live_endpoint`),
    waiting at most 30 s, else exit 1 `not-live` with the window left standing; the window's appearance gets 5 s
    (polling `clients` at 100 ms), then `unplaced`. Each new bound lands as a row of its own beside the full
    time-bound lists.
  - **Words and exits (F6):** exit 2 outside the allowlist (clap's usage error, plus one fixed line for a word after
    `--` other than `claude`, beside `PAIR_AFTER_DASHES`); exit 1 `terminal-not-found`; exit 1 `not-live`;
    `already-live` / `stale-heartbeat` read before any spawn; exit 1 `strict-modes-failed` before any log; no exit 11;
    `--json` `{"v":1,"ok":{"name","parent","window","placement"}}` / `{"v":1,"error":"<code>","detail":null}`; help
    `setup:  open, run, revive, verify, plugin install`.
  - **Parent default:** the parent defaults to the caller's `VIOLA_NAME` when an agent calls open from its own shell.

- **The recorder's three untested codes** (carry `cry-pu3g6nb7`): tests for `viola-hypr-tap`'s `record-move` failure
  codes `move-refused`, `move-unseen` and `window-left`, with no live window, over the planted stubs
  `crates/viola-e2e/tests/hypr_tap.rs` already uses. Each is reachable over a stub variant as the carry names it
  (verified: research M7).

- [premise-corrected: research M1–M3] `split-carry.md`'s seam counts are moved at HEAD `d7b65a6d`: 8 requests (5
  queries, 3 dispatches), 8 words, 5 error words, 9 fixture files, `HYPRCTL_DEADLINE` 5 s settled (was 6 · 6 · 5 · 7
  and PROVISIONAL). Its §5 reached rows are re-read at P3 (`founder-forks.md` block).

- The seam's move dispatch is `hl.dsp.window.move({ workspace = N, window = "address:0x…" })`, recorded by R1 (exit 0,
  stdout `ok`) and replayed by the fake on that exact argv (verified: research M4).

- The seam has no product caller at HEAD — `Cargo.toml:174` under `[dev-dependencies]`; this chunk makes it one
  (verified: research M5).

- Unmeasured live, staying the fake's until R2: the window's map time after the spawn, whether foot maps its window
  before its child runs, a locked desktop's effect on a new window, and a move of a window the product opened (R1
  moved the tap's own); `exec_cmd`'s shell question is moot, no exec being issued (verified: research M6, §What stays
  the fake's).

edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-11-23-viola-open-2 · **Version:** viola-0.2.0
- **Capabilities:** v2-08 claimed, verified on the fake; v2-07 claimed GATED on R2 (carry `cry-fhabylf6`, F9).

- **Binding answers:** F1 · F2 · F4 · F6 · F8 · F9 (the operator's) and F3 · F5 · F7 (the overseer's), cited from
  `split-carry.md` §4 (sealed run `2026-11-23T12-02-15Z-phase`); the technical leans T1–T6 of
  `.andromeda/runs/2026-11-23T21-24-59Z-phase/founder-forks.md` §3, each its ★ arm. The directive is `inputs#I1`.

`viola open <name> [--parent <name>] [--role overseer|builder|worker] [--cwd <dir>] [--workspace N] [--model M]
[--effort E] [--json] [--home H] -- claude` starts a new `foot` window running `<pinned viola> --home H run <name> …
-- claude`, spawned directly with no shell, and returns once the instance is live (at most 30 s). The wrapper of the
new instance finds its own window by its parent pid (the foot process) through the Hyprland seam, moves it to the
target workspace `open` computed (the parent's, or `--workspace N`), and records `window {address, workspace,
placement, origin}` in its first snapshot and one log-only `window` line after `launch`. Off Hyprland the window
still opens, placement reads why. The parent defaults to the caller's `VIOLA_NAME`, which also makes the origin
`agent` (else `cli`).

The launch authority is bounded (v2-08): a flag outside the closed allowlist, or a word after `--` other than
`claude` alone, is refused before anything is read or started; no shell line is built from any argument; the security
decision entry naming the surface, the allowlist and the agent path is the wrap's amendment, the claim standing on
this chunk's own by-construction enumeration (step 26). The seam gets its first product caller, so
`HYPRCTL_DEADLINE` joins the a11y time-bound rows as a row of its own (carry `cry-2oejf2md`), and the tap's three
untested `record-move` codes get tests over planted stubs (carry `cry-pu3g6nb7`).

Per architecture (· decision/run-start-order), (· decision/no-shell-out), (· decision/hyprland-seam-crate),
security-plan (· decision/launch-flags-checked), (· decision/lineage-parent-authenticates-nothing), test-plan
(· decision/fakes-for-external-services), (· decision/single-writer-state-files), a11y-plan
(· decision/time-bounds-fall-on-the-driver). R2 — ONE `viola open` end to end beside a live parent under a scratch home
— is the operator's at his host; implement builds and greens everything else, makes no window and STOPS before it.

title: A. The closed words and the kind — `crates/viola-core/src/lib.rs`, `crates/viola-core/src/obs.rs` (keeps tests S1, S4; security S2)

data.head: ### A. The closed words and the kind — `crates/viola-core/src/lib.rs`, `crates/viola-core/src/obs.rs` (keeps tests S1, S4; security S2)

body:
1. `EventKind::Window`, kebab `window`, keys exactly `address`, `workspace`, `placement`, `origin`; log-only (not in
   the wait-waking set); the kind/key table test gains its row.

2. Two closed word sets beside the kind, each `is_code_word`: `PLACEMENT_WORDS` = `placed` · `unplaced` ·
   `window-unseen` · `unsupported` · `unreachable` · `oversize` · `malformed` · `refused`; `ORIGIN_WORDS` = `cli` ·
   `agent`. A unit test pins both lists literally.

3. `crates/viola-core/src/obs.rs`: the process subject `terminal`; the exit details `terminal-not-found` and
   `not-live`. `schemas/diag-line.v1.json` gains the subject and the two details (step 24).

title: B. State — `crates/viola-state/` (keeps tests S1, S2, S4; security S2)

data.head: ### B. State — `crates/viola-state/` (keeps tests S1, S2, S4; security S2)

body:
4. `crates/viola-state/Cargo.toml` takes `viola-hyprland` (path) for `is_address` alone (Constraints: the one address
   validator). `snapshot.rs`: `Window {address: Option<String>, workspace: Option<i32>, placement: String, origin:
   String}` and `InstanceSnapshot.window: Option<Window>` (`serde(default, skip_serializing_if)`).

5. `replay.rs`: `apply_window_line` in the one pass — a `window` line whose `placement` and `origin` are closed words
   sets the held window (address kept only when `is_address`, workspace only as an i32), the last one winning; a
   `launch` line clears the held window (T6). Cases `window_rule_the_last_line_after_launch_wins`,
   `window_rule_a_later_launch_clears_it`, `window_rule_drops_a_line_with_an_unknown_word`.

6. `board.rs`: the item gains `window?` (`{address, workspace}`, only when the address re-parses through
   `is_address`) and `origin?` (only an origin word). Cases `board_read_item_with_a_window_serialises_it`,
   `board_read_drops_a_window_address_that_does_not_parse`.

7. `liveness.rs`: `ancestors(pid, max)` — the pid's parent chain through sysinfo, at most `max` pids, none past pid 1;
   pids stay in memory. Case `ancestors_of_this_process_start_with_its_parent`.

title: C. The wrapper's window step — `src/run/window.rs` (new), `src/run/mod.rs`, `src/cmd/run.rs` (keeps tests S1, S3; obs S2, S3; security S2)

data.head: ### C. The wrapper's window step — `src/run/window.rs` (new), `src/run/mod.rs`, `src/cmd/run.rs` (keeps tests S1, S3; obs S2, S3; security S2)

body:
8. `src/run/window.rs`: `WINDOW_WAIT` 5 s and `WINDOW_POLL` 100 ms (F8); `window_step(read, terminal_pid, place,
   origin, wait)` over an injected read of the seam: poll `Request::Clients` until a window's `pid` is
   `terminal_pid`; a read error word (`unsupported` · `unreachable` · `oversize` · `malformed`) ends the step at once
   with that word and no address; none seen by `wait` → `window-unseen`; seen with `place` given → one
   `Request::MoveToWorkspace(address, place)`: `Reply::Dispatched` → `placed`, workspace `place`; an error →
   its word, workspace as seen; seen with no `place` → `unplaced`, workspace as seen. One span `run.window`
   (fields `outcome` only). Cases (rstest, injected read): `window_step_moves_the_window_of_its_terminal_to_the_place`,
   `window_step_with_no_place_is_unplaced`, `window_step_with_no_window_is_window_unseen`,
   `window_step_off_hyprland_is_unsupported_at_once`, `window_step_with_a_refused_move_is_refused`.

9. `src/cmd/run.rs` `RunArgs`: two hidden flags (`hide = true`) — `--origin <WORD>` (an origin word, else clap's usage
   error) and `--place <N>` (an i32; `--place` without `--origin` is a usage error in `checked`). Both pass to
   `Launch`; `revive` hands neither.

10. `start`: under `--origin` only, after `trust_folder` and before the slots, run the window step with the resolved
    `hyprctl` on `PATH` (none → `unsupported`, no spawn), `std::os::unix::process::parent_id()`, the place and the
    R8 strip's removal list; `Recorded` gains `window`; `start_state` writes it into the first snapshot and appends
    one `window` line (`source: wrapper`) after the `launch` line. A start with no `--origin` writes no window and
    no line. Cases `start_state_writes_the_window_line_after_the_launch_line`,
    `run_args_refuse_a_place_without_an_origin`, `run_args_take_a_hidden_origin_and_place`.

title: D. The verb — `src/cmd/open.rs` (new), `src/cmd/mod.rs`, `src/human/hints.rs` (keeps design S1, S2, S3; layouts S1, S2, S3; a11y S1, S4; security S3)

data.head: ### D. The verb — `src/cmd/open.rs` (new), `src/cmd/mod.rs`, `src/human/hints.rs` (keeps design S1, S2, S3; layouts S1, S2, S3; a11y S1, S4; security S3)

body:
11. `OpenArgs` (clap): `name` (`parse_name`), `--parent` (`parse_name`), `--role` closed to `overseer|builder|worker`
    (`value_parser` over the three words), `--cwd <dir>`, `--workspace <N>` (i32), `--model` / `--effort`
    (`run::parse_model` / `parse_effort`), `--json`, and the program words after `--` (`last = true`, required).
    `checked`: the words after `--` must be exactly `claude` — anything else is one fixed raw usage line
    `OPEN_PROGRAM` («viola open starts claude alone: put 'claude' after '--' and give viola's own flags before it»),
    exit 2, echoing none of the words; a `--parent` equal to the name is run's self-parent line. Cases (rstest):
    `open_args_take_the_allowlist`, `open_args_refuse_a_word_after_dashes_other_than_claude` (`claude --x`, `sh`,
    `claude; x`, `$(x)`, a word with a newline), `open_args_refuse_a_role_outside_the_three`,
    `open_args_refuse_a_self_parent`.

12. `Command::Open` in `src/cmd/mod.rs`, dispatched with `resolved_home`, its sink `cli` into the opened name's
    `cli-<name>.ndjson`; `HELP_TEMPLATE` `setup:    open, run, revive, verify, plugin install`.

13. `open`: (a) `run::checked_exe` on the home tree — a refusal is exit 1 with run's pair, or under `--json`
    `{"v":1,"error":"strict-modes-failed","detail":null}`, no log; (b) the `cli` log opens, span `cli.open`;
    (c) `collision_check` over `read_snapshot_or_replay` (run's own): `already-live` / `stale-heartbeat` exit 1 before
    any spawn, the json document through `refused_with`; (d) `pin_bytes` places or re-hashes the pinned copy (T5),
    a mismatch `pinned-hash-mismatch`; (e) the parent: `--parent`, else `client::own_name()` dropped when equal to the
    name; origin `agent` when `own_name()` is a name, else `cli`; (f) the target: `--workspace N`, else
    `parent_target` (step 14), else none; (g) `foot` resolved on `PATH` through `run::resolve_program` — absent → exit
    1 `terminal-not-found` (pair + hint, or the json document), nothing spawned; (h) the spawn (step 15); (i) the live
    wait (step 16).

15. The spawn: `Command::new(foot)` directly, argv exactly `--app-id=viola.`, `--title=`, `--working-directory=` (`--cwd`, else the open's current dir, made absolute), ``, `--home`, ``, `run`, ``, then `--parent

` and `--role ` when present, `--model ` / `--effort ` when given, `--origin `, `--place ` when a target stands, `--`, `claude`; stdin, stdout and stderr null, `process_group(0)` so a Ctrl-C to the caller ends no window. One `process-start{subject:"terminal", child_pid}`; the open never reaps foot. `open_argv(…)` is a pure function, case `open_argv_is_the_closed_argv_one_element_each` (a name, cwd and role holding spaces and quotes stay single elements).

16. The live wait: every 100 ms `live_endpoint` on the instance, for at most `OPEN_LIVE_BOUND` 30 s (F8), and foot's
    `try_wait` — foot ended before live reads `not-live` at once. Live → read the snapshot's `window` and print: human
    stdout `<name>  live  <placement>`; `--json` `{"v":1,"ok":{"name":…,"parent":…|null,"window":{"address",
    "workspace"}|null,"placement":…}}`; exit 0. Not live → exit 1 `not-live`, the window left standing: pair `unable:
    <name> did not come up within 30 s` / `hint: the window stays open; viola list shows <name> once it is live`, or the
    json document. Pure `wait_live(probe, bound, poll)`, case `wait_live_past_its_bound_is_not_live` (bound 200 ms).

17. `src/human/hints.rs`: the `terminal-not-found` pair (`unable: no foot terminal on PATH` / `hint: install foot, the
    terminal viola open starts`) and the `not-live` pair (step 16), ASCII, no SGR.

body:

data.head: ### H. Readers of the moved literals and contracts (keeps tests S4; security S3; a11y S1)

body: 22. `tests/cli_output_plain.rs` `HELP`: `setup:    open, run, revive, verify, plugin install`.

    notes §R2). Implement reports and stops; the gated entry stays deferred.

The block runs the formatter and the linter; each touched crate's units; the filtered new-case entries (each selects
only this chunk's new cases: 0 on the untouched tree, read red-vacuous at baseline); the integration binaries the
chunk moves; the supply-chain bans (a dependency edge moves); the host read; the harness's three layers; then the
operator pass.

**What is not run, and why:** no round and no live entry — R2 is the operator's act, outside this block, after
implement's stop (`inputs#I1` item 5); no mutation run (`inputs#I1` item 10); no fuzz target (the new reads are a
`clients` reply through the seam's existing parse, and closed words a bounded events read already parsed). The start
gains a step only under `--origin` (a boot-path touchpoint, `start`): the harness boot smoke runs in the operator
pass, unchanged in shape. The new test binary `tests/cli_open.rs` does not exist on the untouched tree, so no filter
names it by `binary(…)`: its cases are selected by `test(/^open_/)`.

**The remove-the-guard controls** are implement's one-shot `gate.py control` runs, never entries, each fired on its
own filtered entry, its case named, `--timeout 900`; each case fails on its own bounded assertion, so a `timeout`
reading would NOT read the guard as held.

body:
- (security) **matrix#v2-08** — an `open` carrying a flag outside the closed allowlist, or any word after `--` other
  than `claude` alone, exits 2 before any home read, log, pin or spawn
  (`open_args_refuse_a_word_after_dashes_other_than_claude`, `open_refuses_a_word_after_dashes_and_reads_nothing`); the
  one spawn hands foot the closed argv, one element per value whatever characters a name, cwd or role holds, with no
  shell (`open_argv_is_the_closed_argv_one_element_each`, `open_spawns_the_terminal_with_the_closed_argv`); the
  by-construction enumeration of the surface, the allowlist, the one spawn site and the agent path is
  `evidence/v2-08-by-construction.md` (step 26), from which the wrap writes the security decision entry.

- (fleet) **matrix#v2-07** — gated: R2. Over the fakes (this chunk): from the CLI and from an agent's own shell an
  open starts foot running the named wrapped session, returns only once it is live, records `window {address,
  workspace, placement, origin}` in the snapshot and one log-only line after `launch`, places it on the target by the
  one move dispatch (`placed`) and records why where it cannot (`unplaced` · `window-unseen` · `unsupported`), and
  names the calling agent as the parent when none is given (step 20's cases). The acceptance's «a new terminal window …
  placed beside its parent's window on Hyprland» is R2's alone: a stand-in never verifies a gated cap.

- (state) the window record replays from the log, the last line after the last `launch` winning, a later start's
  `launch` clearing it (`window_rule_*`); `list --json` items carry `window?` / `origin?`, an address that does not
  re-parse dropped (· decision/snapshot-replay-fields, · contract/viola-list-json/items).

- (cli) `viola --help`'s `setup:` row reads `open, run, revive, verify, plugin install` (`cli_output_plain`); the two
  new exit-1 codes are code words with one hint each (`cross_exit_causes`); every open document is a named body
  (`contract_error_bodies`); every line written is schema-checked (`contract_diag_schema`, step 20).

- (carry `cry-pu3g6nb7`) the tap's `move-refused`, `move-unseen` and `window-left` each have a test over a planted stub,
  exit 1, nothing written (step 21).

- (carry `cry-2oejf2md`) `HYPRCTL_DEADLINE` (5 s) stands as an a11y time-bound row of its own, with the open's 30 s
  live wait and the 5 s window wait (Expected amendments).

- (tests) every entry of the block above reads green but the gated one, and the three remove-the-guard controls read
  `holds` (`evidence/remove-the-guard.md`).

- architecture · decision/run-start-order · decision/snapshot-replay-log-fields-only · contract/instance-snapshot/data ·
  contract/wrapper-event-appends/launch · decision/event-kinds-agent-neutral · decision/hyprland-seam-crate ·
  decision/no-shell-out · decision/window-features-target-hyprland · contract/cli-exit-codes/1 · /2.

- security-plan · decision/launch-flags-checked · decision/run-lineage-flags-checked ·
  decision/lineage-parent-authenticates-nothing · decision/launch-pair-kept-to-snapshot-and-event-log ·
  decision/hyprland-reply-text-dropped · decision/parent-identity-env-stripped.
- design-system · contract/help-output/verb-groups · contract/viola-help/verb-groups · decision/no-spinners-in-verb-output.
- layout-templates · contract/viola-list-json/document · decision/json-on-every-data-verb · decision/hints-name-next-verb.

- test-plan · decision/snapshot-replay-fields · contract/viola-list-json/items · contract/run-start-events/order ·
  decision/fakes-for-external-services · decision/single-writer-state-files.
- obs-plan · decision/launch-line-untraced · contract/diag-subject/hyprctl-probe · decision/distinct-detail-code-per-exit-cause.

- a11y-plan · decision/time-bounds-fall-on-the-driver · decision/time-bounds-never-on-human ·
  contract/cli-help/served-verbs-only.
- Research files inspected: research.md §Files inspected (16 reads); measurements M1–M11.

- Placement through Hyprland's `exec` or a desktop terminal resolver — each builds a shell line (split-carry §3); foot is
  spawned directly.
- The open writing the window record — only the wrapper writes the snapshot and its start lines (T1).
- A new channel method to hand the placement to the wrapper — a new listener surface needing its own security entry (T1 c).

- A second copy of the address validator in `viola-core` or `viola-state` — the seam crate holds the one
  (security-plan §Input Validation's named exception); `viola-state` takes `viola-hyprland` for it.
- Any env read to detect Hyprland (`HYPRLAND_*`, `TERMINAL`, `WAYLAND_DISPLAY`) — the seam's own word decides (F5).
- A live start, a window, a key or a dispatch during implement — R2 is the operator's.
- Waiting on foot's exit or reaping it — foot outlives the open by design.

- **Basis of the counts:** 8 requests · 8 words · 5 error words (`crates/viola-hyprland/src/lib.rs@d7b65a6d`); 9 fixtures
  (`ls fixtures/hyprland/0.56.2/`); the move fixture's argv and reply (M4); `WINDOW_WAIT` / `WINDOW_POLL` mirror the
  tap's (`crates/viola-e2e/src/bin/viola-hypr-tap.rs:48-49`).

- **Mechanism (step 20's placed case):** the fake foot writes `foot-pid` before it spawns its child; the wrapper's
  `parent_id()` is that pid, since the fake runs `viola run` as its direct child; mode `terminal` prints that pid on
  `0x555aa16bde50`, and `--workspace 1` makes the wrapper's move argv byte-equal to M4's recorded `args`, which the fake
  replays `ok` → `Reply::Dispatched` → `placed`. A target other than 1 would miss the fixture (exit 1 → `unreachable`).

- **The live bound in tests:** a success case is live well inside `WITHIN` 12 s (the window step's worst case on the
  fakes is `window-unseen`'s 5 s); `not-live` is proven at unit level with a 200 ms bound (step 16), never by a 30 s
  e2e wait.

- **R2 (the operator's, after implement's stop; directive item 5).**
  - *Opens:* ONE `viola open`, once. The parent is a `viola run parent -- bash` the operator starts in a foot window he
    opens himself; in that shell he types `viola --home <S> open child -- claude` (origin `agent`, parent defaulted).
  - *Scratch home `<S>`:* a fresh directory under `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` (outside every repository), holding
    `config.json` `{"v":1,"claude_env_keep":["CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR"]}` and a private 0700 `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` beside it,
    exported in the parent's shell.
  - *Needs absent:* `verify_new_cli` (M9: no automatic verify, so the 30 s bound holds) and any instance named `parent`
    or `child` under `<S>`. *Needs present:* `foot` and `hyprctl` on `PATH`, `hyprctl locked` reading `false`. The
    no-start entry reading them: `test ! -e <S>/config.json || ! grep -q verify_new_cli <S>/config.json; command -v
    foot hyprctl; hyprctl locked`.
  - *Leaves:* the child window (foot, its wrapper, claude at its first screen, no key typed), the parent window, `<S>`
    (instances, pinned copy, plugin, diagnostics), the private config dir, the two sockets under
    `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/viola/`. Closed by the operator closing both windows (each wrapper ends with its child), then the
    two scratch dirs removed by name at his desk.
  - *Reads, then writes `evidence/r2.md`:* `viola --home <S> list --json` (the child's `window`, `origin` `agent`,
    parent `parent`), `hyprctl -j clients` (the child's address present, its `pid` the foot pid, its workspace the
    parent window's), the child's `window` line. Red when: open exits non-zero; `placement` is not `placed`; the

29. **The no-start probe (spends nothing of R2's cap):** ONE firing of the test-only recorder's existing move record,
    `viola-hypr-tap record-move --program /usr/bin/hyprctl --terminal /usr/bin/foot --workspace 1 --out
    <scratch>/probe`.
    - It runs with `hyprctl locked` read first and recorded beside it.
    - It opens ONE foot window (app-id `viola.hypr-tap`, running `sleep 30`, no claude), moves it once to workspace 1,
      reads it there through `clients`, kills and reaps the foot it started, and waits until the window is gone.
    - It sends no key and dispatches no focus.
    - Green: exit 0 and one `MoveToWorkspace.recorded-1.json` under `<scratch>/probe/0.56.2/`, the only file it leaves.
    - Red: exit 1 with `viola-hypr-tap: no-terminal-window` (no window within 5 s), `move-refused`, `move-unseen` or
      `window-left`.
    - Its evidence is `evidence/probe-under-lock.md`: the lock reading, the call's line, the verdict word.
    In the block it is the operator entries after the CI read: the build, `hyprctl locked`, then the probe's
    `record-move`.

30. **The no-start preconditions entry, then R2** — the last two operator entries. **The branch line:** R2 fires only
    when the probe entry read exit 0 AND the `hyprctl locked` entry fired just before it read `true`, at the overseer's
    go, once; otherwise R2 does not fire, and the lock read, the preconditions and R2 are fired in the operator's
    morning window. **The two branches (`inputs#I3`):**
    - **probe green under the lock** (and R2 needs no key, no eye, no focus change — Implementation notes §R2) → R2 runs
      ONCE on the locked desktop, at the overseer's go;
    - **probe red, or not run under a lock** → no start; R2 waits for the operator's morning window (about ten
      minutes, his word).
    - A red R2 is final either way: no second start, and v2-07 stays claimed GATED.

title: I5-relay-open2-p5-review.md.txt
body:
# Relay — P5 card 1 of «`viola open`» (2026-11-23-viola-open-2): review, four plan changes

Read by the overseer at 2026-11-23T23:01Z against the card and plan rev 6, both whole. The design, the claims, the
controls and the block stand. Four changes, all in steps 28–30 and their entries; then a new card.

1. **The probe is a READING, never a red.** A locked desktop may honestly refuse to map or move a window: that is
   the question the probe asks, not a failure of the chunk. As written the probe entry has no `expect`, so a
   `no-terminal-window` under the lock reads the operator pass red. Give it `expect = []` (as the lock read has)
   and have the branch line read its recorded exit and verdict word; `evidence/probe-under-lock.md` holds both
   readings. If the tool has no way to record a non-zero exit as a reading, say so and stop — do not wrap the
   command to force exit 0 without printing its real exit.
2. **The morning branch fires the probe AGAIN first, unlocked, and R2 only on its green.** As written, a probe red
   under the lock leads to R2 in the morning with no green probe before it — the one capped start spent on a
   path nothing has shown to work. State the morning order: lock read (either reading) → probe → preconditions →
   R2 only when THAT probe read exit 0. A probe red on the UNLOCKED desktop is a finding: no start, stop, report.
   The night branch is unchanged: probe exit 0 AND the lock read `true` → R2 once at the overseer's go.
3. **Say exactly where implement stops and who fires what** — steps 28–30 and the card read two ways. The order
   to write: the operator pass runs its entries through the CI read; then the build entry; then it STOPS and
   reports, the scratch home and the private config dir made, the R2 ledger line NOT yet written. On the
   overseer's go it fires the lock read and the probe and reports the two readings in one line. On a second go
   it writes the ledger line from `date -u`, fires the preconditions entry and R2, copies the verdict line into
   `evidence/r2.md` and reports. Say what the operator pass's record holds when the window ends with R2 unfired,
   and how the morning firing re-enters (the same window resumed, or a named door of the letters) — if the
   letters give none, say so on the card.
4. **The preconditions entry reads a present config.** `! grep -q verify_new_cli …/config.json` is true when the
   file is absent (grep exits 2). Add `test -f` on it before the grep.

Unchanged and confirmed: the three controls and their entries, entry 16 and its typed control, the amendments
list, the cap of ONE start with no spare, workspace 1. Re-run the checks the edits reach and show card 2.

28. **Where implement stops, and who fires what (`inputs#I5` change 3).**
    - **Implement** builds and greens every non-leg entry and reports; it fires no operator entry, as ever.
    - **The operator pass** fires its entries in block order through the CI read (smoke, pre-push, hygiene, the
      pre-CI commit and push, the CI read), then the build entry. It then makes the scratch home
      `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/viola-r2/home` (with its `config.json`) and the private `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/viola-r2/claude-config`
      (0700, empty) by hand, and **STOPS and reports**. The R2 ledger line is NOT yet written.
    - **First go (the overseer's):** the pass fires the lock read, then the probe, and reports the two readings in one
      line: `lock <true|false> · probe exit <rc> <word>`, the word `ok` on exit 0, else the tap's stderr code from the
      probe's log. Both readings go into `evidence/probe-under-lock.md`.
    - **Second go (the overseer's, only on the branch line below):** the pass writes the R2 ledger line into
      `evidence/r2.md` from `date -u`, fires the preconditions entry, then R2, copies R2's verdict line into
      `evidence/r2.md`, and reports.

29. **The no-start probe is a READING, never a red (`inputs#I5` change 1; it spends nothing of R2's cap).**
    - It is ONE firing of the test-only recorder's existing move record, `viola-hypr-tap record-move --program
      /usr/bin/hyprctl --terminal /usr/bin/foot --workspace 1 --out <scratch>/probe`, with `hyprctl locked` read just
      before it.
    - It opens ONE foot window (app-id `viola.hypr-tap`, running `sleep 30`, no claude), moves it once to workspace 1,
      reads it there through `clients`, kills and reaps the foot it started, and waits until the window is gone.
    - It sends no key and dispatches no focus.
    - Its entry carries `expect = []`. A locked desktop may honestly refuse to map or move a window, and that refusal
      is the question the probe asks, not a failure of the chunk. The tool reads such an entry `recorded · exit {rc}`
      whatever the exit (gate-contract.md §Operator entry, *The line*), and the tap's verdict word stands in its log.
    - Exit 0 leaves one `MoveToWorkspace.recorded-1.json` under `<scratch>/probe/0.56.2/`. Exit 1 carries
      `viola-hypr-tap: <code>`: `no-terminal-window` (no window within 5 s), `move-refused`, `move-unseen` or
      `window-left`.

30. **The branch line (`inputs#I3`, `inputs#I5` change 2).**
    - **Night (the desktop locked):** R2 fires only when the probe read `recorded · exit 0` AND the lock read just before
      it read `true`, at the overseer's second go, once.
    - **Morning (anything else):** no start that night. In the operator's morning window the pass fires, in this order:
      the lock read (either reading), the probe AGAIN, the preconditions, and R2 only when THAT probe read exit 0.
    - **A probe that is not exit 0 on the UNLOCKED desktop is a finding:** no start; the pass stops and reports.
    - A red R2 is final either way: no second start, and v2-07 stays claimed GATED.
    - **When a window ends with R2 unfired:**
      - The record holds, under `.andromeda/cache/chunks/2026-11-23-viola-open-2/evidence/`: each fired operator
        entry's line, `operator-pass.md`, `probe-under-lock.md` (its readings, once fired), and no `r2.md`.
      - Entry 16 stays deferred, and v2-07 stays claimed gated.
    - **The morning re-entry:** the same entries fired by number, `gate.py run --chunk 2026-11-23-viola-open-2
      --operator {n}`, from whatever window the operator opens. The record lives in `evidence/`, not in a window.
      - The letters name no door for an operator pass split across two windows. They name only the gated door
        once the chunk is wrapped `gated`: `/andromeda-implement` in its gated mode, its `--void 16:block cleared —
        {evidence}`, then `/andromeda-wrap-session`.
      - This is stated on the card.

body:
- **R2 (the operator pass's, after implement's stop and the probe; `inputs#I1` item 5, `inputs#I3`).** The cap is ONE
  live `claude` start, with no spare.
  - **Prepared before the window** (no claude, nothing of the cap):
    - the build: `cargo build -p viola` and `cargo build -p viola-e2e --bin viola-hypr-tap`, no `fake-agent` feature;
    - the scratch home `<S>` = `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/viola-r2/home` and the private `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/viola-r2/claude-config`
      (0700, empty), outside every repository; `<S>/config.json` =
      `{"v":1,"claude_env_keep":["CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR"]}`, with no `verify_new_cli`;
    - then, in step 28's order and never ahead of it: the lock read and the probe at the first go (re-fired first in
      the morning order); the R2 ledger line in `evidence/r2.md`, stamped by `date -u`, and the no-start preconditions
      entry at the second go, just before R2.
  - **The no-start preconditions entry** reads:
    - absent: `verify_new_cli` in `<S>/config.json` (M9: no automatic verify — a fresh home holds no stamp, and without
      the key no six verify runs start), and `<S>/instances/parent` and `<S>/instances/child`;
    - present: `foot`, `hyprctl` and the built `viola` (`command -v`); `hyprctl locked` (recorded, either reading);
    - `df -m /tmp`.
  - **The parent it stands beside:** `parent`, a `viola run` wrapping `/usr/bin/sleep 900`, no claude. R2's command
    starts it inside a foot window of its own (foot spawned directly) and waits for it to read `live`. Under W1 (a) it
    starts with the hidden `--origin cli --place 1`, so its own wrapper moves it to workspace 1 and records its window.
  - **The one command, verbatim:**
    `bash scripts/r2-open.sh "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/viola-r2/home" target/debug/viola`.
    It (1) starts the parent's foot and waits for `parent` to be live (bound 30 s); (2) runs
    `viola --home <S> open child --parent parent --json -- claude` — the ONE claude start; (3) reads `viola --home <S>
    list --json` and `hyprctl -j clients`; (4) prints `r2: <verdict> placement=<word> workspace=<n|none>
    parent_workspace=<n|none>`; (5) closes the child's foot and the parent's foot by the pids it read (the child's from
    `clients`' `pid` at its recorded address; the parent's its own child) through the EXIT trap, on every exit path,
    and waits until both windows are gone (5 s each).
  - **Green** (`r2: green`): open exit 0, `placement` `placed`, the recorded address in `clients` with the foot pid,
    and its workspace equal to the parent window's. **Red:** anything else, with the first failing reading named.
  - **Leaves:** `<S>` and the private config dir (instances, pinned copy, plugin, diagnostics, what claude wrote at its
    first screen) and the two sockets under `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/viola/`; each is named on the card and removed by name at
    the operator's desk, never by a recursive delete of the session's.
  - **The CLI is unverified under `<S>`** (no stamps): transport only, no trust record written, claude's own first screen
    left unanswered. «Live» is the wrapper's first snapshot and beat, which precede the claude spawn (M10), so claude's
    own start time is outside the 30 s bound.

title: I6-implement-open-directive.md.txt
body:
# Implement directive — «`viola open`» (chunk 2026-11-23-viola-open-2)

The plan is approved (P5 card 2, plan rev 7). This window is fresh: read the chunk's documents from the store and
its evidence dir from disk first. This directive is the only file of its folder you read or snap.

**In your own chat messages never print a compiled screen literal verbatim**: name it. Call no scheduled-wake or
timer tool. **NO mutation run and NO witness run. Until the operator pass's first go, NO window is opened, moved,
focused or closed, NO key is sent and NO real `claude` is started. The only window acts of this chunk are the
probe's and R2's, each on the overseer's own go; the only real `claude` start is R2's ONE, no spare.** Nothing of
the operator's real `~/.claude*` is read or copied — R2's private config dir stays empty.

## The host — another project works here

- The filtered entries run as they come. **Before the three whole layers (unit, integration, e2e) and again before
  `pre-push`: read `hostwatch.py read --last 15`** (`~/dev/projects/additional/andromedaV3/andromeda-overseer/docs/tools/hostwatch.py`)
  and `df -m /tmp` beside it. QUIET → go on. CONTENDED naming a NEIGHBOUR alive in the stalled seconds → STOP and
  say in one line which entries wait; the overseer arranges a quiet window and sends the word with the time to
  read hostwatch FROM. A CONTENDED reading where only this run's own build was alive is none: go on.
- A gate red where no assertion failed on a value (a stall, a timeout, a kill) is read against the same record
  first and never re-run for green into a contended host: say so and wait for the overseer's word.
- Read `df` before any step that rebuilds whole.

## Stops

- **The plan's order is the order.** Implement builds and greens every non-leg entry, writes
  `evidence/v2-08-by-construction.md` and `evidence/remove-the-guard.md`, and never runs `scripts/r2-open.sh`.
- **The three controls** are fired by `gate.py control` with the plan's `--timeout 900`, each on its own filtered
  entry. A case that cannot be made to fail with its guard removed stops implement for that site.
- **No new closed word, exit, flag, request, time bound, environment read, record field or fake mode beyond the
  plan's:** a need for any stops implement and is the operator's — he is away, so it is written to the run's
  `founder-forks.md` with its options priced and the step stops there.
- A filter that still selects 0 tests after its step is a red, said so. A sweep of a counted literal (event kinds,
  the help's verb row, the exit-detail lists, the snapshot's recovered list) reads the test tree's strings too.
- A red that would move a plan entry stops implement before the operator pass: say which entry and why.
- A guard's or the permission classifier's refusal is never routed around: stop and say so. On an account-limit
  refusal, stop where you are. Remove no scratch clone or test dir by a recursive delete: name it in the report.
- Every TEST start runs under a test-owned user home and runtime dir, and every test ends the stand-in terminal
  and the wrapper it started. No leaf gains a figure the code states. No master row is reworded in this skill.

## On green — the operator pass, with its two goes

Write the chunk report (P4), saying plainly what stands unproven behind R2. Then start the operator pass in this
same window as plan step 28 orders: its entries through the CI read (`ci.py conclusion`, leg=operator), then the
build entry; make the scratch home with its `config.json` and the empty 0700 private config dir; **then STOP and
end the turn with one line: where the pass stands, the CI verdict, what is made.** Do not wait in a loop.
- **On the overseer's first go:** the lock read, then the probe, ONCE; report `lock <true|false> · probe exit <rc>
  <word>`; write `evidence/probe-under-lock.md`; end the turn.
- **On the overseer's second go, and only then:** the ledger line from `date -u`, the preconditions entry, R2
  ONCE; copy its verdict line into `evidence/r2.md`; report the line verbatim and what stands on disk outside the
  tree, each thing by name. A red R2 is final: no second start, no retry of any part of it.
- If no second go comes, write the pass's record as it stands, say R2 is unfired, and end the turn.
End every process you start.

title: evidence/v2-08-by-construction.md
body:
# v2-08 — the launch authority bounded, by construction Read from the tree of implement run `2026-11-23T23-08-26Z-implement` (uncommitted on `d7b65a6d`), for the wrap's security decision entry. Ranges are copied from that run's new-text listing (`.andromeda/runs/2026-11-23T23-08-26Z-implement/new-text.md`). ## The argument surface — every `OpenArgs` field and its parser (`src/cmd/open.rs:40-69`) | field | flag | parser | what passes | |---|---|---|---| | `name` | positional | `super::send::parse_name` | a `ViolaName`: `[a-z0-9-]`, 1-32 chars, a letter first | | `parent` | `--parent ` | `super::send::parse_name` | a `ViolaName`; equal to `name` refused in `checked` (exit 2) | | `role` | `--role ` | clap possible values `["overseer", "builder", "worker"]` | one of the three words | | `cwd` | `--cwd ` | clap's `PathBuf` | any path; made absolute (`std::path::absolute`) and handed as ONE argv element | | `workspace` | `--workspace ` | clap's `i32` | an integer; handed as `--place `, one element | | `model` | `--model ` | `super::run::parse_model` (`viola_core::is_model_word`) | a model word | | `effort` | `--effort ` | `super::run::parse_effort` (`is_effort_level`) | one of the five effort words | | `json` | `--json` | flag | — | | `program` | after `--` (`last = true, required = true`) | `checked`: exactly `["claude"]` | the word `claude` alone | The global `--home` is the CLI's own (`src/cmd/mod.rs`, `resolved_home`). Any other flag is clap's unknown-argument usage error (exit 2) before `open` runs: `open_args_take_the_allowlist` reads `--home-dir` and the wrapper's hidden `--origin` both refused `UnknownArgument`. ## The allowlist — the words after `--` (`src/cmd/open.rs:71-87`, `checked`) `args.program != [OsStr::new(PROGRAM)]` (`PROGRAM` = `"claude"`) is one fixed raw usage error, `OPEN_PROGRAM`, exit 2, echoing none of the words. `checked` runs first in `open` (`src/cmd/open.rs:89`), before `checked_exe` reads the home, before the `cli` log, the pin and any spawn. Witnesses: `open_args_refuse_a_word_after_dashes_other_than_claude` (`claude --x`, `sh`, `claude; x`, `$(x)`, a word holding a newline, `claude claude`) and, end to end, `open_refuses_a_word_after_dashes_and_reads_nothing` (exit 2, the fixed line, no foot receipt, the home never created). Its remove-the-guard control is `open-allowlist` (`evidence/remove-the-guard.md`). ## The one spawn site — no shell - `spawn_terminal` (`src/cmd/open.rs:326-344`): `Command::new(foot)` with `.args(argv)`, stdin/stdout/stderr null, `process_group(0)`; `foot` is the absolute path `run::resolve_program` found on `PATH` (none: exit 1 `terminal-not-found`, nothing spawned). - `argv` is `open_argv` (`src/cmd/open.rs:292-324`): `--app-id=viola.`, `--title=`, `--working-directory=`, the pinned viola, `--home`, ``, `run`, ``, then `--parent

`, `--role `, `--model `, `--effort ` each when present, `--origin `, `--place ` when a target stands, `--`, `claude` — every value one element, built from the checked fields alone. Witnesses: `open_argv_is_the_closed_argv_one_element_each` (a cwd and a home holding spaces and quotes stay single elements) and `open_spawns_the_terminal_with_the_closed_argv` (the stand-in foot's argv receipt equals the closed argv). - The grep, run over the file: `command grep -nE '"sh"|"bash"|"-c"|/bin/sh|Command::new' src/cmd/open.rs` → `330: let child = Command::new(foot)` and `435: #[case::a_shell(&["sh"])]` — the second the refused word inside the allowlist's own test module. No `sh`, `bash` or `-c` is built anywhere in the file. - The compositor reads go through the seam alone (`viola_hyprland::read`, the program resolved on `PATH`, a closed argv), the same as every other caller. ## The agent path — origin and the parent default - `caller = client::own_name()` (`src/cmd/client.rs:209`): `VIOLA_NAME` parsed as a `ViolaName`, self-reported. - `origin` (`src/cmd/open.rs:127`): `agent` when `caller` is a name, else `cli` — a closed word handed as `--origin`, authenticating nothing (the wrapper re-checks it against `ORIGIN_WORDS` in `run`'s `parse_origin`). - `parent` (`src/cmd/open.rs:128-131`): `--parent`, else `caller`, dropped when it equals the opened name. Witness: `open_from_an_agent_shell_names_the_caller_as_parent` (the lineage line's parent is the caller, the window line's origin `agent`, `--parent overseer` on foot's argv). - The window record (`window {address, workspace, placement, origin}`) is written by the started wrapper alone, into its first snapshot and one `events.ndjson` line after `launch`; no process-log line carries an address, a pid or a workspace (`run.window` holds `outcome` only).

# Relay — `scripts/r2-open.sh` before any go: two mends, then the first go

Read by the overseer at 2026-11-23T23:49Z: the script whole, CI ci#45290221248 green 7 of 7 on `5155468a`. The
pass's stop is right. No go is given yet — the one capped start runs unattended on a locked desktop, so the
script is mended first. Both mends are in the script alone; no product file moves.

1. **A red path can leave the child's window standing.** `child_foot` is set only from the address in the open's
   own `ok` document. On `open` exit 1 `not-live`, on `window-unseen`, on any reply with no address, it stays
   empty; `end_wrapper child` then helps only if a snapshot with a live pid exists. The window of the ONE claude
   start may stay open on the operator's desktop until morning — the opposite of «closes what it opened on every
   exit path». Mend: when no address gave a pid, find the child's terminal another way the script itself can read
   (the compositor's clients by the app-id the open sets, `viola.child`; and the processes whose argv is the
   script's own child `run` line under this scratch home) and close it by the same `close_foot`. After cleanup
   the script reads clients once more and appends ` left=<n>` to the verdict line when any window of app-id
   `viola.parent` or `viola.child` still stands (nothing appended when none) — a reading, not a new red.
2. **A green that never saw the agent proves less than the start it spends.** «Live» precedes the agent's spawn,
   and the script closes the window the moment the open returns, so the one `claude` may never have started.
   Mend: before the verdict, wait up to 20 s for the child wrapper's own agent child to exist (read it the way
   the tree lets a script read it — the wrapper's pid from the child's snapshot and its child process; say which),
   and append ` agent=<comm|none>` to the verdict line, green or red. It is a READING: it turns no green red,
   and the plan's expect atom (`contains r2: green placement=placed `) still holds. No key is sent to it.

Then: `bash -n` and shellcheck on the script; a dry read of both new paths WITHOUT a window or a claude (over
planted files or the fake, your choice — say which); the fix commit, the push and its CI read as the pass orders a
change after the pre-CI commit; hygiene again. Report in one message what changed and the new CI verdict, and
**then fire the FIRST GO in the same turn: the lock read and the probe, ONCE**, and end the turn with the line
`lock <true|false> · probe exit <rc> <word>`. The second go is NOT given by this relay.

**Section:** Standard Contracts
**Change:** ~ decision/snapshot-replay-log-fields-only · rule: was «A snapshot rebuilt by replay recovers only links, agent_session_id, wheel, lineage and launch from the log; a field no line gave is absent, never a default.»; now «A snapshot rebuilt by replay recovers only links, agent_session_id, wheel, lineage, launch and window from the log; a field no line gave is absent, never a default.»
